comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Credit Portfolio Credit Losses and Reserves
comparisons.peer_summary: Net charge-offs for the consumer portfolio increased by $1.1 billion to $4.2 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher credit card loan charge-offs, while the allowance for loan and lease losses remained relatively unchanged at $8.6 billion compared to 2023. The macroeconomic environment during 2024 featured stable U.S. unemployment rates and steadily increasing home prices.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America reported increased net credit losses in their consumer credit portfolios for 2024, primarily driven by credit card loan performance. Citi attributes its year-over-year increase to the maturation of recent card vintages and macroeconomic pressures on lower FICO customers. Similarly, BAC reports a $1.1 billion increase in consumer net charge-offs, explicitly stating this was 'primarily due to higher credit card loan charge-offs.' While Citi highlights the specific mechanism of vintage maturation delayed by pandemic stimulus, BAC focuses on the aggregate dollar increase in the consumer portfolio.

sentences.text: The net credit loss rate increased year-over-year, primarily reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years.

In addition, the increase was driven by macroeconomic pressures related to the elevated inflationary and interest rate environment impacting both cards portfolios, with lower FICO band customers primarily driving the increase.
Net charge-offs increased $1.1 billion to $4.2 billion in 2024 primarily due to higher credit card loan charge-offs.
